**Contract deviations: none.** Two implementation notes for downstream owners:

1. `errors.mjs` declares each class as a *named class expression* exported under the contracted binding, e.g. `export const PyValueError = class ValueError extends PyException {}`. So `err.name === 'ValueError'` **and** `err.constructor.name === 'ValueError'` **and** `err.stack` starts with `ValueError: msg` — both readings of the contract comment are satisfied, and the JS global `TypeError` is not shadowed. `instanceof PyException` / `instanceof Error` / subclassing all work normally. `PyException`'s own name is `'Exception'`; the name is derived via `new.target.name`, so any further subclass reports its own name (mirrors `type(exc).__name__`).
2. `encodeSurrogateescape` — CPython raises `UnicodeEncodeError` for a lone surrogate outside U+DC80..U+DCFF. Throwing from a byte-level writer would break stderr reporting, so those emit U+FFFD instead (documented in the file). Unreachable in this program: `repr()` escapes every `Cs` code point to ASCII before anything is written, and U+DC80..U+DCFF round-trip exactly.

`\p{Unassigned}` **is** accepted by this Node (v18.19.1, V8 10.2, ICU 74.2 / Unicode 15.1), so no fallback was needed; the regex uses the equivalent short alias `\p{Cn}` inside one module-level character class `[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]/u`, with U+0020 special-cased as printable. CPython 3.12 ships Unicode 15.0 vs Node's 15.1 — they agree on every code point exercised.

CONTRACT: no deviations in export names/signatures. Three implementation choices worth flagging:

1. `writeStdout`/`writeStderr` use `fs.writeSync(fd, …)` in a partial-write loop, not `process.stdout.write`. The assignment suggested the stream API; the stream is async whenever fd 1/2 is a pipe, so `exit()` could truncate. With writeSync every byte is on the fd before `exit()` runs, so `exit()` is just `process.exitCode = code; process.exit(code)` with no flush dance. Loop handles EAGAIN (1 ms `Atomics.wait` backoff, for a non-blocking inherited fd), EINTR (retry), and swallows EPIPE/EBADF silently (documented in-file). node:fs was already needed for /proc, so no new bare import; `builtins.mjs` has zero bare imports.

2. `writeStderr` applies Python's **backslashreplace** error handler before encoding. Empirically confirmed against the reference: CPython's `sys.stderr` cannot UTF-8-encode a lone surrogate, so an undecodable argv byte surfaces as the literal ASCII text `\udcff`, not as raw byte 0xff — `test3_executable --a 5 --b x $'\xff\xfe'` prints `unrecognized arguments: \udcff\udcfe`. A plain `encodeSurrogateescape` write would have emitted raw bytes and mismatched on every `unrecognized arguments:` / `ambiguous option:` message carrying invalid argv bytes. `reprStr` output (already ASCII-escaped) is unaffected — no double escaping. `writeStdout` keeps `encodeSurrogateescape` per the contract.

3. `getTerminalColumns` imports `pyIntFromString` from `./int.mjs` instead of a local ad-hoc integer parse. The reference genuinely applies full `int()` semantics to COLUMNS (verified: `COLUMNS=٢٠`, `２５`, `2_0`, `" 20 "` all re-wrap the help; `20.0`, `1e3`, `abc`, `0`, `-5`, `""` all fall back to 80). int.mjs is already a hard dependency of the program via types.mjs, so this adds no new failure mode; every throw is caught → 0. Values above 2^31-1 are clamped (unobservable: that already means "never wrap") to keep the formatter's padding maths finite.

**One spec-detail correction (required for byte-exactness)**
The assignment said to build the usage wrap units as "optParts (per optional action)". CPython 3.12 `_format_usage` instead re-splits the joined usage string with
`part_regexp = r'\(.*?\)+(?=\s|$)|\[.*?\]+(?=\s|$)|\S+'`, so a *required* (unbracketed) option splits into two parts: `--a A` → `['--a', 'A']`. Only bracketed/parenthesised groups stay whole. This is observable: at `COLUMNS=40` the reference emits

```
usage: test3_executable [-h] --a A --b
                        B
```

which the per-action variant cannot produce (it would break before `--b`). I implemented the regex split; everything else (`get_lines`, the 0.75·width prog-leading test, the `lines.length > 1` re-flow, `help_position`/`help_width`/`action_width`, `_split_lines` + greedy textwrap, empty-section suppression, `_long_break_matcher` + strip) follows the spec/CPython as written.

**Verified against the reference binary** (scratch harness `/tmp/fmtcheck.mjs`, which imports the module and diffs against `COLUMNS=n /workspace/dataset/test3_executable`, with `prog='test3_executable'`):

- Result: **413 widths × 2 streams, all byte-identical.** `COLUMNS` unset / `0` / `garbage` all resolve to 80 columns (width 78) when stdout is a pipe, matching `shutil.get_terminal_size()`.

Notes for the parser owner: `formatUsage` returns no trailing newline, so the error path is `formatUsage(...) + '\n' + prog + ': error: ' + msg + '\n'`; `formatHelp` returns the complete document ending in exactly one `\n`. `formatHelp` derives `action_max_length` from the actions inside `groups` (mirroring `add_arguments` per section) and uses the flat `actions` list only for the usage line.
